why: It was written for the 2017 Taipei City Government ChatBot contest, answering city-service questions on Facebook Messenger and LINE from the city's own FAQs. It was not selected, which left nine years for a rewrite. This one has no server and no bots, and every answer still points back to the agency that wrote it.
gains: For a Taipei resident with a city-service question: ask in everyday words (狗, not 犬) and get the official FAQ with its agency, date and page, so you can judge whether it still applies. Free mode costs nothing; AI mode bills your own key and shows how much.

lessons: "身分證不見了" (my ID card is gone) used to rank a lost house-number plate first: the colloquial 不見 outweighed 遺失, the city's word. Synonyms now count as one idea.
A Chinese embedding model would add about 38 MB of downloads, over 15 times the gzipped FAQ file, so meaning is left to the optional AI mode.
Word matching has limits: asking about moving to Mars (火星移民) lists questions for new immigrants, thanks to the word 移民.
subtitle: City-service answers, with sources
description: Search 8,000-plus Taipei city-service FAQs in your browser. Every result links back to its source; an optional model-assisted mode can summarise the answers.
longDescription: The 2017 Taipei city-government chatbot competition project, rebuilt in 2026 as a static web app. Chinese BM25 retrieval runs locally in a Web Worker and returns the issuing agency, date and source for each FAQ. An optional mode uses your own API key to summarise the retrieved material.
features: Agency, update date and original source on results
Chinese retrieval in a Web Worker
Optional answers grounded in retrieved FAQs
